document_check.note: The document is Pappalettera C, Nucci L, Cacciotti A et al. (2025) 'Electroencephalography-based signatures of cognitive resilience in individuals with stable mild cognitive impairment despite carrying a high-risk for progression to dementia', Alzheimer's Dement (TRCI) 11:e70194. It is an INTERCEPTOR sub-study comparing baseline EEG in 60 sMCI-resilient, 56 cMCI and 50 healthy controls. It reports a healthy-like delta profile and a higher alpha-2 small-world index in the resilient group, as cited.

cited_result: Baseline resting EEG differences between high-risk MCI participants who stayed stable over 36 months (sMCI-resilient) and those who converted to dementia (cMCI). The resilient group had a healthy-like delta profile, frontal alpha enhancement and stronger anterior alpha coherence, and a higher alpha-2 small-world index, which the authors propose as possible correlates of resilience.
tool_reason: The cited result is the association of baseline EEG features, measured prospectively and analysed feature by feature rather than as a model, with later conversion versus stability in a cohort. That is a prognostic-factor question. A JBI case-control reading of the same outcome-defined comparison would raise the same confounding problem.

domains.rationale: Screening and enrolment counts are given, and MCI follows NIA-AA criteria. Inclusion and exclusion criteria, recruitment sites and period are only in the supplement or earlier papers, not in this document. The analysed subgroup (hippocampal atrophy plus FDG-PET positive, n = 116) was chosen because it had the highest conversion rate in this same cohort. The healthy controls were recruited outside the project from an undescribed source.

signalling.question: Adequate participation of eligible persons and description of source population?
signalling.quote: A total of 494 MCI subjects gave their consent to participate in the study and were screened for eligibility, 398 of whom were finally enrolled.

signalling.question: Inclusion and exclusion criteria described?
signalling.quote: Inclusion and exclusion criteria can be found in the Supplementary Materials.

signalling.question: Was the condition defined by standard criteria?
signalling.quote: The core criteria for MCI diagnosis were defined according to the National Institute on Aging Alzheimer’s Association workgroups.

signalling.question: Was the analysed subgroup selected independently of the outcome data?
signalling.quote: The subgroup showing the highest conversion risk was further subdivided into individuals who converted to dementia and those who remained stable or reverted to normality.

signalling.question: Source and recruitment of the comparison (healthy) group described?
signalling.quote: A group of 50 healthy controls (HC) recruited outside the Interceptor project was included specifically to provide a comparative benchmark.

signalling.question: Baseline sample described?
signalling.quote: The demographic and lifestyle characteristics and relative p-value are shown in Table 1.

domains.rationale: The 11.8% lost at baseline are reported. Losses during the 36-month follow-up, reasons for loss, and whether stable participants completed the full follow-up are not reported, so misclassifying drop-outs as stable cannot be excluded.

signalling.question: Response and baseline loss reported?
signalling.quote: Of these, 47 (11.8%) were lost at baseline. Ultimately, 351 participants were included in the analysis and followed over 3 years

signalling.question: Loss to follow-up during the 36 months reported, with reasons?
signalling.quote: Searched Methods and Results for dropouts, withdrawals, deaths or incomplete 36-month follow-up among the 351 or the 116; none reported.

signalling.question: Participants lost compared with those retained?
signalling.quote: Searched for characteristics of participants lost; none reported.

domains.rationale: The EEG protocol (19 channels, eyes closed, at least 5 minutes, at least 3 minutes clean) is stated, but processing details are only in the supplement. The document does not report acquisition sites, equipment harmonisation across centres or for externally recruited controls, or whether processing was blind to conversion status. Frequency-band limits are inconsistent between Methods, Results and figure legends.

signalling.question: Clear definition and method of measurement of the prognostic factor?
signalling.quote: Each participant underwent resting-state EEG recordings in an eyes-closed condition (EC) for at least 5 min using 19 electrodes, positioned according to the International 10–20 System.

signalling.question: Same method and setting of measurement for all participants?
signalling.quote: Searched Methods 2.2 for recording sites, equipment and harmonisation, including for the externally recruited HC; details deferred to Supplementary Materials.

signalling.question: Measurement blind to outcome?
signalling.quote: Searched for blinding of EEG processing to conversion status; none reported.

signalling.question: Consistent definition of the factor across the report?
signalling.quote: delta (2–4 Hz), theta (4–8 Hz), alpha 1 (8–11 Hz), alpha 2 (11–13 Hz)
signalling.page: 4 (vs 'In the delta band (1–4 Hz)', p5, and 'alpha 1 (8–10 Hz), and (C) alpha 2 (10–12 Hz)', p7)

domains.rationale: Conversion was assessed with 6-monthly neuropsychology, but the dementia criteria are not given in the document and the outcome is all-cause dementia. The 10 reverters were counted as stable. With a fixed 3-year window, late converters are classed as 'resilient', which the authors acknowledge. Blinding of the diagnosis to EEG is not reported.

signalling.question: Clear definition and valid method of outcome measurement?
signalling.quote: Neuropsychological evaluations were performed every 6 months to assess the main cognitive domains and support the determination of conversion to dementia.

signalling.question: Is the outcome category homogeneous?
signalling.quote: 85 (24.2%) participants converted to a clinical diagnosis of AD and 19 (5.4%) progressed to other clinically defined forms of dementia

signalling.question: Was stability classified appropriately?
signalling.quote: These subjects were thereafter included in the stable group in the further analyses.

signalling.question: Was follow-up long enough to classify stability?
signalling.quote: it cannot be excluded that some of the MCI subjects with a resilient EEG pattern who remained stable at the end of the follow-up, despite carrying one or more risk factors could progress to dementia later.

signalling.question: Outcome assessed blind to EEG?
signalling.quote: Searched for blinding of clinical diagnosis to EEG results; none reported.

domains.rationale: Converters had worse baseline cognition (MMSE 24.5 vs 26.04) and more family history. EEG slowing tracks disease severity, so the stable-versus-converter differences may reflect how far the disease had progressed at baseline rather than resilience. The primary EEG comparisons are unadjusted t-tests. The adjustment claimed in the Discussion is not described in the Methods (which describe only Pearson correlations), its results are not shown, and it concedes that only 'the majority' of features were robust.

signalling.question: Important potential confounders measured?
signalling.quote: Demographic, clinical, and lifestyle characteristics included age, sex, years of education, family history of dementia, and smoking status.

signalling.question: Were groups balanced on key confounders?
signalling.quote: Global cognitive performance measured by MMSE was significantly lower in the cMCI group and intermediate for the sMCI-resilient group.

signalling.question: Important confounders accounted for in the primary analysis?
signalling.quote: For EEG analyses, relative PSD and delta/alpha ratio were compared between groups (healthy, sMCI-resilient, and cMCI), electrode by electrode using independent samples t-tests and applying false discovery rate (FDR) correction to account for multiple comparisons.

signalling.question: Is the adjustment reported in the Discussion described in the Methods?
signalling.quote: Initially, a multiple regression analysis including all covariates was carried out. Results suggested that, although some trends are observable, the majority of EEG features were robust enough to the potential confounding effects such as age, sex, education, family history, and baseline cognitive performance.

signalling.question: What confounder check do the Methods describe?
signalling.quote: Before performing the EEG analyses, Pearson’s correlation analyses were carried out to assess whether demographic and clinical variables influenced the EEG metrics.

domains.rationale: Many measures, bands and electrodes (or electrode pairs) are compared. Coherence was tested with pairwise electrode-pair t-tests with no stated multiplicity correction. The small-world ANOVA used Duncan post hoc tests, which are liberal. No effect sizes, time-to-event or prognostic estimates are reported. The small-world statistic is internally inconsistent: F(6, 672) = 2.3572 corresponds to p of about 0.03, not 0.00001, and 672 error degrees of freedom imply about 115 participants rather than the 166 analysed.

signalling.question: Was the analysis appropriate for the design, with multiplicity controlled?
signalling.quote: In the coherence analysis, connectivity maps of healthy, sMCI-resilient and cMCI were examined with pairwise t-tests between electrode pairs to identify significant differences in functional connectivity.

signalling.question: Were post hoc procedures appropriate?
signalling.quote: When significant main effects or interactions were observed, Duncan post hoc tests for multiple comparisons were applied.

signalling.question: Are reported statistics internally consistent?
signalling.quote: The results revealed a significant interaction effect between all factors (F[6, 672] = 2.3572, p = 0.00001)

signalling.question: Is there no selective reporting?
signalling.quote: The mean values and standard errors for each electrode and for the significant frequency bands are reported in Tables S8–S10.

overall_rationale: Under QUIPS, any high domain gives an overall high rating, and two domains are high. Confounding is high because baseline cognitive severity differs between stable and converting participants and the primary EEG comparisons are unadjusted. Statistical analysis and reporting is high because of the many uncorrected or liberally corrected comparisons and an internally inconsistent key test statistic. Participation, attrition, EEG measurement and outcome classification (a fixed 3-year window, reverters counted as stable) add moderate concerns.
